page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the N2 server family. It is configured with 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The instance features 32.0 GB of dedicated system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place the n2-standard-8 primarily in the average tier for general computing tasks. It achieves average scores in multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and software compilation. However, single-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the lower 25th percentile. Similarly, specialized workloads such as ray tracing, image processing, and prompt processing for small language models show weaker performance. Conversely, tasks like Redis SET operations, static web serving, and text generation for small language models maintain average throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density make this instance suitable for workloads requiring predictable performance without the premium of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware. The lack of local storage and GPU capabilities limits its utility for high-performance storage-heavy databases or machine learning training. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, standard database operations, and moderate text processing tasks.
